subject: Post-demo: decision criteria clarification + proposed test plan
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: decision criteria clarification + proposed test plan

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and a suggested next steps list so we stay aligned with your procurement and technical teams.

Top pain points you reiterated:
- Unpredictable token costs on peak traffic (esp. batch processing for nightly reports)
- Latency spikes during concurrent workflows (~95th percentile requirements)
- Need for audit logs and compartmentalized data retention for compliance

Business goals you shared:
1) Migrate inference for the summarization pipeline to a predictable, capped cost model for Q3
2) Meet a 99th percentile latency target of <350ms for 512-token requests
3) Ensure auditability for PHI-handling flows (SLA + retention policy)

Competitive context (from our side):
- Vendor A: strong latency on shortseqs but higher token cost with no integrated KV caching
- Vendor B: cheaper nominal rates but limited model variants and no private deployment option

Open questions we heard from your side:
1) Which tests will demonstrate cost stability versus peak concurrency?
2) How long of a KV-cache warmup is realistic for your workload shapes?
3) Do you need dedicated capacity (single-tenant) or is an isolated tenancy sufficient?

Proposed immediate next steps (we recommend starting this week):
- RW comparison spreadsheet (attached) — we scored decision criteria vs the two vendors you mentioned
- 48–72h live tests:
  * Cost-under-load: run a synthetic workload to 10k requests/hour with representative prompt distribution
  * Latency SLA run: measure p50/p95/p99 for 256/512/1024 token runs
  * KV/cold-start characterization: repeated prefix hits to observe warmup curve
- Deliverable: consolidated run metrics + recommended config (quantization, batch size, routing policy)

Can you confirm:
A) who on your side will own the live-tests (name/email)
B) whether procurement needs a stamped SOW before we start the tests

I attached a short recommended-test-plan and a one-page vendor comparison table for quick review.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min working session if useful.

—Olga
Olga Petrov

Olga —

Appreciate the concise recap. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- Test owners: Technical lead will be Priya Shah (pri.shah@cardinalhealth.com); she'll own the coordination for the latency and KV tests. Procurement will be CC'd on scheduling.
- Procurement note: We don't need a stamped SOW to begin these discovery tests, but we do need an NDA addendum to cover the sample PHI-like payloads. Procurement (procurement@cardinalhealth.com) will send over the addendum.

Quick ask re the test plan: can you add a short column in the comparison sheet showing the expected unit-cost per 1M tokens for the baseline config? That will help our finance partner triage quickly.

We'll aim to start the tests Tue or Wed next week — Priya will propose slots.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex / Priya / team —

Thanks — added a unit-cost column to the comparison workbook and a short timeline in the test plan. Link and attachments below. Key changes:
- Unit-cost estimates (baseline config) are conservative — include batching and minimal KV-caching assumptions
- Test duration: each run is ~48 hours to capture diurnal variability; we recommend at least one weekend run for noise isolation
- Security: we'll stand up an isolated test endpoint inside your VPC for PHI-like payloads; logs will be limited to hashed identifiers only unless you opt into full retention

Attachments: redwood-demo-notes.pdf (one-pager), updated rwinference_vs_vendor_table.xlsx
Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/file/d/1A2B3C/review-sheet

Next steps — proposed schedule:
1) NDA addendum from procurement (you indicated today) — once received, we can provision the endpoint
2) Priya proposes Wed/Thu time windows for an initial 2-day run
3) We will share a lockfile & run script and ask for a single point of contact to trigger the tests

Marissa / Rishi — can you both review the test script (attached) and flag anything that will materially change runtime cost estimates?

Olga
